logs.detail: Malformed request pattern matching known CVE-2026-XXXX exploit attempt logged but not blocked (WAF rule not yet deployed).
Remote code execution achieved on unpatched application server. Patch had been available for 47 days.
Outbound reverse shell connection established from web server to external IP.
High-priority alert generated for anomalous outbound connection from server subnet.
Alert reviewed within SLA, immediately escalated to IR due to high-priority classification.
Webshell removed, server patched and hardened.
Server validated and returned to production behind updated WAF rule.

Initial Access.what_happened: Attacker exploited a known, unpatched vulnerability on a public-facing server.
chain: Why was the server exploitable? -> A publicly known vulnerability (CVE) was left unpatched.
Why was it unpatched? -> The patch had been available for 47 days without being applied.
Why wasn't it applied in that window? -> No enforced SLA for critical patch deployment.
Why is there no enforced SLA? -> Patch management is manual and not prioritized by CVSS/exploitability.
Root cause: Lack of an enforced, risk-based patch management SLA.

Detection Gap.what_happened: WAF logged the exploit attempt but did not block it.
chain: Why wasn't the request blocked? -> No WAF rule existed yet for this specific CVE pattern.
Why was there no rule? -> WAF rule deployment lagged behind vulnerability disclosure.
Why did it lag? -> No process to fast-track virtual patching via WAF when a real patch is delayed.
Root cause: No virtual-patching process to cover the gap between vulnerability disclosure and actual patch deployment.

corrective_actions.action: Implement enforced patch SLA tied to CVSS score, with automated tracking

corrective_actions.finding: No WAF rule to virtually patch known CVE during exposure window
corrective_actions.action: Establish a virtual-patching process to deploy WAF/IPS rules within 24-48 hours of CVE disclosure

what_worked_well: SIEM correctly flagged the anomalous outbound connection as high-priority immediately.
SOC analyst triaged and escalated within SLA, unlike the previous incident.
Containment and eradication were completed within 2 hours of detection.

lessons_learned_meeting.key_takeaway: Detection and response performance was strong once the exploit occurred, which validates recent SLA improvements. The real gap is upstream: patch management timelines and lack of virtual patching left a 47-day exposure window that should not have existed.
